outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: both parallel and serial failed with 58 of 70 tests passed. The serial run avoided shared-output coordination costs and kept a cleaner one-owner lifecycle, while the parallel run had to recover from an overwritten entrypoint. The pair evidence supports that as a realized adverse parallel process episode, but not as a cause of an outcome difference because the final official result is the same and the available summaries do not expose the 12 hidden failing cases.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used multiple live children that wrote competing /output implementations, causing entrypoint repair and extra verification before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept discovery, implementation, integration, and verification in one thread and avoided shared-output collisions.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both artifacts likely retained a Bech32/CLI semantic mismatch on hidden cases, but the pair contains only aggregate official results and not per-case diagnostics.
File organization and naming differed between the two implementations without changing the official pass/fail relation.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator summary gives aggregate 58/70 results for each mode; it does not identify hidden failing cases inside the allowed pair evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained parallel pattern explains process rework but not a distinct official outcome
